access_links.label: City of Paris Cours Oasis page

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the City of Paris OASIS programme, which turns sealed asphalt schoolyards into green cool islands open to pupils and, outside school hours, to vulnerable neighbours such as the elderly. It followed the 2003 heatwave, which caused nearly 1,100 deaths in Paris, and the June 2017 heatwave during school time; Paris schools have 73 hectares of sealed yards, and central residents have about 6 square metres of green space each. After a first test in 2018, the Urban Innovative Actions project (2019-2021) transformed ten pilot yards, four kindergartens, four elementary and two middle schools, chosen by social vulnerability, microclimate and technical criteria, with trees, lawns, gardens, light porous surfaces and other natural elements, co-designed with pupils and staff through CAUE 75 workshops. The ERDF contribution was about 5.0 million euros, and the citywide programme spends about 9 million euros a year on around 25 yards, co-funded by the city, the State and the Seine-Normandie Water Agency. The page, published in 2022 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal with links to the city and UIA pages. Caveats: guards, cleaning and neighbour noise complaints add costs and limit weekend opening, and cooling is not quantified on the page. It illustrates green and blue infrastructure for climate adaptation to extreme heat at critical facilities; related records are the Stuttgart ventilation corridors and Vitoria-Gasteiz green infrastructure case studies.
name: Paris OASIS schoolyard greening programme
outcomes: Ten pilot schoolyards were greened and several opened to the public as cool islands, and the city now funds about 25 yards a year from a standard methodology.
